We need evaluate each of BC-001 to BC-069. Need likely many have extra wording issues (e.g., "so that It is easier to use", "links to slides", duplicate "so that", implementation hints, "must accept", etc.). Minimal violation means story contains more than role, means, optional ends/rationale. Many user stories have extra clauses/requirements/notes within story sentence, such as "The following information must be shown: ...", "Trainers can see all class attendance at first because...", "The URL path should be SEO friendly..." etc. Need classify Violation when core story includes comments/mock-up notes/impl details/procedural notes/other information external to story sentence. But we need avoid penalizing grammar or other QUS criteria unless relevant. Extra text about "and links to slides" after rationale? That's not role/means/ends, violation. Additional info "The following information must be shown" in BC-015/016 is mock-up/note/requirements embedded. Violation. We must produce evidence and rationale.

Need define exact story IDs and decisions.

Let's list stories and assess.

BC-001: "As a anonymoususer, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all the awesome sponsors." Classic role means ends. No extra. No violation.

BC-002: "As a anonymoususer, I want to view a list of user profiles, so that I know who is attending the conference." Classic. No violation.

Means has "from website for info and updates"; ends "so that It is easier to use." The rationale maybe weak, but minimal not about quality of rationale. No extra. No violation. Does "for info and updates" count means? It is part of means. No violation.

It might be intended as additional requirement, external to story sentence. Means: edit my training node myself. Ends: coordinators don't have to. "and links to slides" is extra, maybe means? Could parse "I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." That "links to slides" is outside role-means-ends. Violation.

But ensure not conflating with Well-formed? Minimal: contains extra "and links to slides" not role/means/ends. Yes Violation. Evidence: "and links to slides" or full.

Contains role "trainee", means "limit to one registration per day per authenticated user". But "per authenticated user" maybe extra clarification, but still means? Ends "we don't have duplicate spaces." No explicit extra. However role as trainee, means about per authenticated user? Does not include comments/impl/testing hint. Maybe no violation. But "per authenticated user" maybe procedural? I think not. No violation.

But check "As a trainee, I want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user" - role and means. No violation.

Contains duplicate "so that, so that" and list "attendend, refunded, no show". Minimal? The core includes repeated rationale and perhaps typo. Is "so that, so that" extra? Not exactly additional info but syntax. "we can see if attendend, refunded, no show" is rationale. The duplicate "so that" is not additional info external? Could be well-formed issue, not minimal. But there's "so that, so that" maybe the story has two "so that" and the phrase after first "so that" incomplete? Actually text: "I want to have an admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show." Core has an extra "so that," but not an extra requirement? Minimal definition: contains nothing more than role, means, and optional ends/rationale. If duplicate connector is redundant, but does it make it contain something more than role, means, ends? No, still role/means/ends with typo. Could no violation. But "attendend, refunded, no show" are examples in rationale. Rationale is acceptable. No violation.

Need be consistent. This criterion not about grammar. So BC-007 No Violation likely.

The "so" duplicate maybe no minimal violation. Pronoun "they" maybe not. No violation? It includes nothing more than role means rationale. No violation.

"with a checkbox" is UI detail, but is that "implementation/testing hint"? Minimal criterion says nothing more than role, means, optional ends/rationale. "with a checkbox" is an implementation/UI hint in the story sentence. Is that external? Yes, specifying checkbox. The means should be "accept cancellation terms"; "with a checkbox" is extra UI implementation detail. Violation. Evidence: "with a checkbox". Also "must accept" maybe procedural but "must" maybe redundancy. We'll decide Violation.

Means includes "that was processed via stripe" as implementation detail? Some might call implementation hint (Stripe), but it describes the money to refund. Is "processed via stripe" extra? That specifies type of money, not how to implement. Is that extra? Hmm.

Mentioning Stripe is an implementation/technology note in story sentence. Could be violation. But role/means may legitimately include a needed condition (money processed via Stripe). However technology mention "stripe" is external. We need decide.

Operationally: Violation when core story includes comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information that should be external to the story sentence. "processed via stripe" is a parenthetical detail of the means. Is it an implementation hint? Maybe yes: "how to process refunds" is via stripe. But it's not an instruction to developer; it's context about which money. Types of sponsorships and payment are domain. I'd be cautious. Let's see user story: "As a administrator, I want to refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe, so that people get their monies back." This follows role-means-ends; the means contains a condition "that was processed via stripe". This is arguably necessary to understand which money, not an external note. Minimal violation should be reserved for clear extra info/comments/notes. I'd say No Violation.
